title: Osmania University Heritage Campus, Hyderabad
tagline: Osmania University Heritage Campus — iconic Indo-Saracenic granite landmark of Hyderabad

overview.short: The Arts College building at Osmania University in Hyderabad is a monumental heritage landmark renowned for its Indo-Saracenic and Nizami architecture.
overview.description: Commissioned in the 1930s by the 7th Nizam of Hyderabad, Mir Osman Ali Khan, and designed by Belgian architect Ernest Jasper, the monumental College of Arts building is an extraordinary blend of Indo-Saracenic, Moorish, and traditional Deccan Hindu-Muslim architectural styles carved from solid pink granite. Set amidst sprawling tree-lined avenues in eastern Hyderabad, it remains one of the city's grandest architectural treasures.

topPlaces.name: Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology
topPlaces.description: The Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (Hindi: कोशिकीय एवं आण्विक जीवविज्ञान केंद्र, IAST: Kośikīya evam āṇavik jīvavijñāna kendra) or CCMB is an Indian fundamental life science research establishment located in Hyderabad that operates under the aegis of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research. CCMB is a designated "Centre of Excellence" by the Global Molecular and Cell Biology Network, UNESCO. The center collaborates with the University of Nebraska Medical Center for translational research on glaucoma.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Osmania Arts College?
faq.a: The best time to visit Osmania Arts College is Oct – Mar. Summers are 26–40°C and winters are 12–28°C.

faq.q: How do I reach Osmania Arts College?
faq.a: The nearest airport is Osmania Arts College / nearest airport (30 km) and the nearest railway station is Secunderabad Junction (Hyderabad) (3 km). Roads are generally good; check seasonal/monsoon conditions before high-altitude or remote stretches.
